scenario: A runaway tram is heading toward ten workers on the main track. Dana can pull a lever that redirects the tram onto a side track, where one worker stands. If she pulls the lever, the tram will kill that worker and spare the ten. If she does not, it will kill the ten and spare the one. Dana cannot stop the tram. Should she pull the lever?

frameworks.reason: The agent assesses Dana’s duty “do not intentionally kill the innocent” toward one worker. Dana is the duty-bearer; one worker is the protected party. The competing obligation being assessed is Dana’s “Imperfect duty to aid” toward ten workers. For “pulls the lever”, the agent proposes the maxim “Pull the lever”. This is an interpretation of possible practical reasoning, not an established intention. Its purpose is Preserve ten lives; its chosen means are Redirect tram onto side track. The proposed justification is: If everyone caused a certain innocent death to avert greater harm, security of persons would erode. The agent assesses the maxim as indefensible, and the action as impermissible. Its proposed means–ends reasoning is: Dana relies on redirecting the tram; the death is foreseen but not relied upon as a causal step. Physical means references: E2; end references: E4. For Dana’s option “pulls the lever”, the ledger records prohibited. The agent’s stated reason is: direct harm to innocent violates perfect duty. The agent assesses Dana’s duty “refrain from killing an innocent person” toward one worker. Dana is the duty-bearer; one worker is the protected party. The competing obligation being assessed is Dana’s “Imperfect duty to aid” toward ten workers. For “does not pull the lever”, the agent proposes the maxim “Do not intervene”. This is an interpretation of possible practical reasoning, not an established intention. Its purpose is Avoid killing innocents oneself; its chosen means are Omit lever pull. The proposed justification is: Refraining from killing to help others can be willed universally. The agent assesses the maxim as defensible, and the action as permissible. Its proposed means–ends reasoning is: Dana refuses to become a killer even though she foresees the tram will kill ten. Physical means references: none; end references: none. For Dana’s option “does not pull the lever”, the ledger records permissible. The agent’s stated reason is: omission keeps hands clean of direct killing.
